findings.location: Bottom identification of f(x) in previous example
findings.observation: The source prints f(x)=x while F(x)=-x²/2 and the preceding ODE is y-prime=-xy.
findings.derivation: F-prime=-x; differentiating a exp(-x²/2) gives -xy. The displayed positive f would instead yield a exp(x²/2).
Substitute a=-2 into y=ax². The printed algebraic relation is not that parabola.

findings.observation: Division requires g(y) nonzero. Examples explicitly restore y=0; the general formula does not list all equilibrium solutions.
findings.resolution: Apply separation on a solution interval where g(y) is nonzero; also test every root g(y0)=0 as the constant solution y=y0.
findings.derivation: The chain rule gives dH(y(x))/dx=y-prime/g(y)=f(x). If g(y0)=0 then y-prime=0=f(x)g(y0). Without regularity/uniqueness, piecewise solutions reaching or leaving roots can require separate study.

findings.observation: H^{-1} is written without specifying branch, interval or range. H=ln|y| is not one-to-one on all nonzero reals.
findings.resolution: Choose a connected y-interval with continuous nonzero g, so H-prime=1/g keeps one sign and H is strictly monotone; restrict x so F(x)+c is in its range.
findings.derivation: For ln|y| the branches give y=+exp(F+c) or -exp(F+c); the initial value selects sign. This supplies the conditions for the source inverse expression.

findings.observation: The ODE and ray slope are undefined at x=0 although the plotted parabolas pass through the origin.
findings.resolution: The ODE solutions y=ax² are defined on intervals avoiding x=0; they admit smooth extensions through 0 as curves, but do not satisfy the displayed ODE there.
findings.derivation: (y/x²)-prime=(xy-prime-2y)/x³=0 for x nonzero, proving completeness separately on either half-line. Constants on the two sides need not agree absent an extension requirement.

findings.location: Example 4 ellipses, reciprocal slope and explicit branches
findings.observation: A genuine ellipse requires c>0. The displayed graph ODE divides by y and the negative-reciprocal argument uses finite nonzero parabola slope.
findings.resolution: For c>0 use smooth implicit ellipses; graph branches have |x|<2sqrt(c) when differentiating. At y=0 use vertical tangent geometry. c=0 is a point and c<0 has no real locus.
findings.derivation: Differentiate x²/4+y²/2=c to get x/2+yy-prime=0; semi-axes 2sqrt(c) and sqrt(2c) have ratio sqrt(2). Where x,y are nonzero, (2y/x)(-x/(2y))=-1. The x-axis member a=0 intersects at y=0 with horizontal/vertical tangents. Ellipse points at x=0,y≠0 do not belong to any finite-a parabola.

findings.observation: The source obtains the correct one-parameter family and separately includes a=0.
findings.resolution: An integrating-factor check proves every differentiable solution is captured, including zeros.
findings.derivation: d[exp(x²/2)y]/dx=exp(x²/2)(y-prime+xy)=0, so y=a exp(-x²/2) on each connected interval. This is an independent supplement, not a source-displayed proof.
